This practical course is for all diploma students of the Technical College.
It builds the digital skills that everyone needs for study, work and daily
life: the apps that make us productive, your university account, cloud
storage and files, **Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint**, and **AI tools**
(such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT and Gemini) to write documents, work with
data and design presentations, safely and honestly.

**A face-to-face course in the computer lab.** Every week has two sessions
of 60 minutes. Each session has three parts:

- **the slides:** first, the teacher explains the new ideas;
- **the worksheet (PDF):** then you practise the same ideas yourself. Part A
  of each experiment is in the real app (Word, Excel, PowerPoint or an AI
  tool). Part B is on a simulator of the interactive lesson. On paper, scan
  its QR code with your phone; on the screen, click its link;
- **the interactive lesson:** the same ideas in short points, the
  simulators, and a check after every step that answers at once.

No lab computer today? Do Part B of each experiment on your phone, and do
Part A later on any computer with Office (or Office on the web at
`office.com`).

**Textbook.** Evans, A., Martin, K. and Poatsy, M. A. *Technology in Action*,
Global Edition, 18th ed., Pearson, 2024. References: Lambert and Frye,
*Microsoft Office Step by Step (Office 2021 and Microsoft 365)*, 2022;
Microsoft 365 Training (support.microsoft.com/training); UNESCO, *Guidance
for Generative AI in Education and Research*, 2023.

## Units

The course in 15 weeks, in teaching order: 10 units and 5 practice weeks,
with two lectures in the lab each week, numbered in one sequence (Lectures
1–30). A unit brings new skills. A practice week (dashed, tagged
*Flexible*) has no new ideas: its two lectures practise the earlier
lectures, and weeks 14 and 15 hold the course project. If a practice week
is not taught, study it at home: every answer is on its page. Faded
sessions are not available yet.
